hook: Page co-founded Google with Sergey Brin in 1998 and served as the company's CEO in two stretches, first from 2011 and again as CEO of Alphabet from its 2015 creation until his 2019 departure. As CEO he led Google's 2014 acquisition of DeepMind and helped fund the company's early Google Brain research.
name: Larry Page

quote.text: Imagine if this kind of intelligence were thrown at your schedule, your information needs. That's what I'm excited about.
quote.context: Larry Page discussing DeepMind's potential, TED 2014

reading.body:
Larry Page's 2014 decision to acquire DeepMind while serving as Google CEO directly positioned the company to lead in AI research before the field's current acceleration.

Page built Google into a search and internet infrastructure company with the capital and scale needed to fund speculative AI research. When he returned as CEO in 2011, he moved quickly to acquire DeepMind in 2014, treating advanced AI capability as a strategic asset worth more than $500 million at a time when most technology companies had not yet identified it as central to their future. This acquisition brought a dedicated AI research team and infrastructure into Google's operations.

The timeline shows a founder retaining decision-making power across organizational changes. Page shaped Google's direction as CEO from 2011, then moved to Alphabet's CEO role when the holding company was created in 2015, before stepping down in 2019. His quoted interest in applying AI to personal information management and scheduling reflected how he saw the technology's commercial potential early. That vision mattered because it channeled Google's existing computational resources and data infrastructure toward AI development at a moment when those assets were not yet constrained by power or building limitations.

This record does not cover Page's views on scaling compute, power demands, or the infrastructure required to run modern AI systems. It shows only that he recognized and funded AI capability when he had the authority to allocate Google's resources toward it.

timeline.event: Co-founds Google with Sergey Brin on September 4, 1998.
timeline.impact: Launches the search engine that becomes the core of Alphabet.

timeline.event: Becomes Chief Executive Officer of Google in April 2011, succeeding Eric Schmidt.
timeline.impact: Returns to day-to-day operating control of the company he co-founded.

timeline.event: Leads Google's acquisition of DeepMind, announced January 26, 2014.
timeline.impact: Brings DeepMind's AI research team into Google ahead of the company's later AI push.

timeline.event: Becomes Chief Executive Officer of Alphabet when the holding company is created in August 2015.
timeline.impact: Moves into an oversight role atop Alphabet's businesses while Sundar Pichai becomes CEO of Google.

timeline.event: Steps down as Chief Executive Officer of Alphabet on December 3, 2019.
timeline.impact: Sundar Pichai becomes CEO of both Google and Alphabet.
